promises.title: You own it
promises.line: We build your site in our GitHub organisation, then move the repository, with its full history, to your own GitHub account: within three months at the latest, sooner if you ask. Until then we hold it for you.
promises.proof: The three months is an expectation we set ourselves, not yet a rule in the terms. After the move the repository is in your name, and nothing of yours stays with us.

promises.title: Nobody can lock you in
promises.line: No platform and no subscription from us, and no terms of ours on how you use your site; only the terms of the services you choose, such as GitHub, your domain registrar and Claude. The code is open source, so nobody can withdraw it, us included.
promises.proof: Sovereignty is not where a site is hosted. It is whether you can move the site, its data and its structure somewhere else, and you can.

promises.title: You change it by talking to Claude
promises.line: Ask your own Claude, the AI assistant, for a change in plain words. A behaviour policy and checks run before anything goes live, and every change can be undone.
promises.proof: Yiheng Wang gave Claude her CV as a PDF; Claude read it and added her latest experience to her site.

promises.title: You can run it anywhere
promises.line: The site is plain files, so any web host can run it, in any region you choose. GitHub Pages is free for a public repository, but not, in [GitHub's own words](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits) (read 19 November 2026), "to run your online business, e-commerce site, or any other website that is primarily directed at either facilitating commercial transactions or providing commercial software as a service (SaaS)". Whether a small business's site falls under that is GitHub's call. For a business site, use a static host whose free plan has no such rule, such as Cloudflare Pages (its [Free plan limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/) and [service terms](https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-developer-platform/), read 19 November 2026), or any paid static host.
promises.proof: Each host's own instructions for putting the site online, linked from one page.

promises.proof: The sites the same team has already made, each labelled as a named person's site or a demo.

promises.title: Almost nothing to attack, and it costs once

promises.proof: Why a static site in your own repository is an alternative to WordPress, Wix and Squarespace, with the vendors' own security figures labelled as theirs.

devices.title: On a device you hold (a plan)

faq.a: A small team of AI agents doing one focused job for you. Each agent has a role, a brief and a behaviour policy that says what it may and may not touch, and the agents work together in your own accounts, where you can see the work and stop it ([the cell is the unit](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-cell-is-the-unit.html)). [What a cell is](/next/cells/) says more.

As big as the job. The smallest is your own website: a team of agents builds it in one session, and a team of six or seven agents inside the site is the next step, not yet built. Bigger cells add a person who helps you, a conductor with its own agents, or a team of people each with their own agents, like ours at Web Summit ([our own team's work](/next/team-work/)).

In your own accounts: your GitHub, your Claude plan, your host and your domain. The smallest cell is built in our GitHub organisation and moved to your account within three months at the latest, sooner if you ask; that is an expectation we set ourselves, not yet a rule in the terms. Running some agents on a Raspberry Pi or an Android tablet is a plan (see the appliance, below).

faq.q: Can I see what a cell does, and stop it?
faq.a: Yes. The work is kept as files and every change is a commit, so you can read who changed what and undo it; in our own cells each commit is also signed by the agent that made it. A person can stop a cell: when we stopped about a hundred of our own agents at once, pausing took seconds, but some agents heard the order late and a few things got through ([stopping a hundred agents](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/stopping-a-hundred-agents.html)). We say that plainly because a stop has to be tested, not assumed.

faq.q: What does a bigger cell cost?
faq.a: Two bigger cells are priced as first proposals: a few sessions with a person, then you run the team yourself; or a team with a conductor, set up in your own accounts. A team for an event, like ours at Web Summit, is priced for each engagement. Nothing at these sizes has been sold. The [pricing page](/next/pricing/) has the first proposals.

faq.q: What is the sovereign website appliance?
faq.a: A plan, not a product yet: a sovereign website on a device you hold, a configured Android tablet or a set of Raspberry Pis that serve the site from home, to be offered through a Kickstarter campaign. Nothing has been submitted to Kickstarter, and the appliance's software is a plan ([launching the appliance](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/launching-the-sovereign-website-appliance.html)).

{launch} once, at the [launch price](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-sovereign-website.html), usually {usual}, with no subscription from us. After that it depends on you. If you edit the site yourself, you need your own Claude plan: Claude Pro is USD 17 a month billed yearly ([Anthropic's page](https://claude.com/pricing), read 19 November 2026). Or a partner edits it, at their price, or you leave it as it is: the site keeps running without edits. Hosting can cost nothing on a host whose free plan fits your site; for a business site, check the host's terms ("Can I move it to another host?" below says more). A domain of your own is paid to the registrar you choose.

faq.q: Can I see one before I pay?
faq.a: Yes. We build a limited number of sites each day free of charge, for evaluation. [Ask for a site]({{contact}}) and say you would like a free evaluation.

You do, once it is handed over. We build it in our GitHub organisation, then move the repository, with its full history, to your own GitHub account within three months at the latest, sooner if you ask; until then we hold it for you. The three months is an expectation we set ourselves, not yet a rule in the terms ([the reasoning](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/fliplet-and-the-website-cell.html)).

faq.q: Can I move it to another host?
faq.a: Yes, whenever you like. The site is plain files, so it runs on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel or any web host. GitHub Pages is free for a public repository, but [GitHub's page](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits) (read 19 November 2026) says it is "not intended for or allowed to be used as a free web-hosting service to run your online business, e-commerce site, or any other website that is primarily directed at either facilitating commercial transactions or providing commercial software as a service (SaaS)". Whether a small business's site falls under that is GitHub's call, not ours. For a business site, use a static host whose free plan has no such rule, such as Cloudflare Pages (its [Free plan limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/) and [service terms](https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-developer-platform/), read 19 November 2026, set usage limits but no rule against business sites), or any paid static host. [Put your site online](https://agenticcells.ai/deploy/) links to each host's own instructions.

faq.q: What if you disappear, or are bought?
faq.a: Once the site is handed over, nothing changes for you. You already hold the files, their history and the instructions for your Claude, and the code is open source, so nobody can withdraw it ([sovereignty you can move](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/sovereignty-you-can-move.html)). Before hand-over the site is in our organisation, which is one reason to ask for the move early.

faq.q: Do I need a GitHub account?
faq.a: Yes, to receive the repository at hand-over. Making one is free, and we point you to the guidance. Until then the site runs on our account so we can finish the work.

faq.q: How do I change the site later?
faq.a: Tell your own Claude, the AI assistant, what you want, in plain words: a new page, a new photo, your latest job from a CV. The site's CLAUDE.md (a short instruction file) and behaviour policy tell Claude how to make changes carefully, the checks run before anything goes live, and any change can be undone. You need a Claude plan for this, or a partner who edits it for you.

Every change is a commit, so any version can be restored. The checks stop most broken or private changes before they go live. A static site is not automatically safe, though: if you want a person to watch over it, a partner can sell you that.
You, with your own Claude, or a partner you choose. We sell no subscription and no support: our part ends when the site is yours.

faq.q: Can I use my own domain?
faq.a: Yes. The site can run on your own domain with HTTPS. Until you have one, it runs on an address of ours. The domain stays registered in your name, with the registrar you choose.

The agents write in your language, and a site can carry more than one. This site's own pages are written in several languages; the translations are made by agents and say so until a native speaker checks them.

There is very little on the site itself to attack: no server code of yours, no database, no plugins, no login page on the site, and no cookies unless you add them. The risks move elsewhere: your GitHub account (use two-factor sign-in), the email account behind your GitHub and your domain registrar, the registrar itself, anyone you give access to the repository, such as a partner, a Claude session misled by something it reads (changes are reviewed and can be undone), GitHub itself (an outage or a suspension), and, until hand-over, our own organisation. The [security page](/next/security/) says more.

The site itself sets no cookies by default and has no tracking of ours. The host keeps its own logs: GitHub says that when a GitHub Pages site is visited, "the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes" ([GitHub's page](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages#data-collection), read 19 November 2026), under GitHub's own privacy statement. Other hosts keep their own logs; you choose the host.

Freelancers, consultancies and firms who sell the site to their customers while we build it. The customer still owns the site; the partner keeps the relationship and may sell hosting, care and changes at their own prices. [The partner terms](https://agenticcells.ai/partners/) are published.

By then the repository should be in your GitHub account and the address pointed where you choose, and we hold nothing. If you asked sooner, it happened sooner. This is an expectation we set ourselves, not yet a rule in the terms.
No. Nothing has been sold yet, and we will say so until it changes. The examples are sites made by the same team, each labelled as a named person's site or a demo.

cell.title: What an agentic cell is
cell.text: A cell is the unit of what we sell: one focused job, done by a small team of AI agents. Each agent has a role, a brief that says what it does, and a behaviour policy that says what it may and may not touch. The smallest cells run in one session; bigger ones span several sessions and people. A cell works in your own accounts, and you can see what it does and stop it ([the cell is the unit](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-cell-is-the-unit.html)).
points: An objective: the one job it exists for, in your words.
A deliverable: what you have at the end, such as a live site, drafted replies or a debrief.
A behaviour policy for every agent: what it may reach, and what it will never do.
Every change is a commit you can read and undo; in our own cells each commit is signed by the agent that made it.
It runs in your own accounts, and a person can stop it.

agentic_web.title: The agentic web
agentic_web.text: The agentic web is sites and services run by teams of agents for the people who own them. In Dinis Cruz's words: "In 2000 the open web gave you software to run yourself; WordPress made publishing free, but you or someone you paid still did the work. In 2026 a team of agents does the work" ([Sovereign Agentic Website](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/sovereign-agentic-website.html), 19 November 2026). The agents work inside a behaviour policy, so what they build stays yours.

The Sovereign Agentic Website (Sovereign Website for short) is the smallest cell we sell, and the clearest example of what a cell does: a team of agents interviews you, makes five designs, puts the site live and hands it over, and your own AI changes it when you ask ([Sovereign Agentic Website](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/sovereign-agentic-website.html)). It is also an open pattern: anyone can use it without paying us.

That is our own team's work, not a customer's, and it is the kind of team a bigger cell sets up.
